strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Moves the next post-fetch Mode Pack provenance-verification route boundary from caller-supplied typed-target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe journey continuation.
Continues an admitted journey through existing headless.run.drive/headless.run.advance authority across a second explicit route boundary while preserving stop-boundary behavior.
Keeps provenance route eligibility, target derivation, checkpoint binding, replay, and denial in the Rust runtime rather than the VSIX or headless caller.
Binds provenance route resume to selected-candidate fetch checkpoint fingerprints and bounded post-route progress so a headless caller can recover from runtime-owned state.
Returns bounded provenance route-resume metadata with source checkpoint fingerprint, derived target class, result continuation, post-route progress, replay state, and next action.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, context_management, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive can accept one explicitly authorized journey_route_resume envelope and derive a selected-candidate provenance-verification target from persisted selected-candidate fetch checkpoint evidence without caller-supplied modepack_selected_candidate_provenance_verification_target.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.2 derives only the selected-candidate fetch target, while M49.3 can dispatch provenance verification only when the caller supplies the typed target. The next trusted route boundary still remained outside Rust-owned journey execution.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller would still need external glue to inspect fetch evidence, build trusted provenance-verification targets, and manage lost-response replay outside the Rust execution authority.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.2 fetch-route resume, M50.1 journey admission, and R7.2 control-plane completion guarding because it crosses the next post-fetch provenance-verification boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The existing headless.run.drive method is extended with one additional bounded journey_route_resume route kind and result metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds executable provenance route continuation, checkpoint validation, ledger evidence, and replay behavior rather than a report, digest, readiness, history, or inspection surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: The Rust runtime validates journey fingerprint, session sequence, route kind, selected-candidate fetch checkpoint fingerprint, provenance evidence availability, authorization, and replay identity; derives a ModePackSelectedCandidateProvenanceVerificationTarget; executes it through existing continuation authority; persists bounded resume evidence; and replays without duplicate route side effects.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can continue a Golden Journey from selected-candidate fetch into provenance verification after a crash or boundary stop without reconstructing trusted provenance target identity in the caller.
answers.milestone_progress: Adds the second runtime-derived post-admission Mode Pack route continuation needed before M50 can reach end-to-end journey completion.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.3 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime provenance route-resume phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one authorized bounded provenance journey-route resume envelope without adding a new RPC

the runtime derives a selected-candidate provenance-verification target from persisted selected-candidate fetch checkpoint evidence instead of requiring caller-supplied modepack_selected_candidate_provenance_verification_target

journey-route resume validates journey fingerprint, current session sequence, route kind, source fetch checkpoint fingerprint, authorization, provenance evidence availability, and replay identity before route side effects

unsupported route kind, missing authorization, stale checkpoint fingerprint, missing checkpoint, missing provenance material, and mixed explicit target requests fail closed without new provenance verification, drive, or resume evidence
replaying the same resume request returns committed bounded metadata without duplicating provenance verification, drive, or journey-route resume ledger evidence

resume result metadata contains bounded journey/task/run/session/drive handles, route kind, source checkpoint fingerprint, derived target class, result advance/continuation id, post-route progress, next action, replay flag, and deterministic resume fingerprint

VSIX validators accept both supported bounded route-resume protocol shapes and reject malformed fingerprints, false authorization, mixed explicit targets, mismatched derived target classes, and raw/unbounded fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, new RPC, or VSIX-owned policy is added

technical_debt: M50.3 supports fetch and provenance route resume; approval, replacement, and closure remain caller-owned until later phases.
The runtime monolith and large behavior-test module remain maintainability risks; module splitting should follow stable behavior slices rather than block Golden Journey capability.

Selected-candidate fetch checkpoint evidence now carries private provenance material for runtime derivation; later phases should preserve bounded RPC/ledger exposure while improving provenance material acquisition ergonomics.
next_capability_rationale: After M50.3 merges, the next distinct M50 phase should derive candidate approval from bounded provenance verification evidence or close a completed journey from runtime state.
Do not add another wrapper around route state; keep moving route boundaries from caller-owned target assembly into Rust-owned replay-safe continuation.
